segments.narration: A ship abandoned in 1931 kept turning up for decades. Empty, drifting, and always gone again before anyone could claim her.
The Baychimo was a 1,322-ton cargo steamer built in Sweden in 1914, run by the Hudson's Bay Company.
In October 1931, heavy with furs, she jammed solid in pack ice off Barrow, Alaska. The crew camped on the ice beside her.
segments.visual_query: ship frozen in alaskan sea ice

segments.narration: A blizzard hit that November. When it cleared she was simply gone, and they took the furs out by air and went home.
She was seen off Alaska for 38 years, boarded more than once, never recovered. The last confirmed sighting was 1969.
